solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boxing in silver martial arts costume is most fitting or least fitting?

indicators.note: boxing something in means enclosing it, so the outer word wraps round the inner pieces

parts.note: the most fitting choice is the best one
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a gi is the loose suit worn for judo or karate

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer wonders whether a karate suit is the perfect fit or the worst one.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reuses 'fitting' on purpose: the question mark lets 'most fitting' sit in the wordplay while its opposite, 'least fitting', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are baggiest hang loosest on the body, so they fit the wearer worst of all.

clue.text: Chap touring Swiss city, ignoring a winter sport

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the man's name goes round the city

parts.note: a bod is British slang for a person

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the city's letter A is disregarded

parts.note: the English spelling of the Swiss city Basel

explanation.surface: A man travelling round a Swiss city skips one of the winter sports on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing a sled down an ice track is the Winter Olympic sport also called bobsleigh.

clue.text: Set on making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word goes back the way it came, read upwards

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A tennis player sets about staging a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: On and leg are interchangeable names for the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set, as a jelly firms up or a team comes together.

clue.text: Relentless boxer, one losing face in battle with Ali

indicators.note: in battle things are thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
the face is the front, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written before its front goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tireless fighter takes a punch in the face during his bout with Muhammad Ali.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexorable means impossible to stop or persuade, so it is a synonym for unyielding and unceasing.

clue.text: Police officer who's taking action to retain power

indicators.note: retaining something means keeping it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: one who sues is taking legal action
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A senior detective goes to court to keep his authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is the informal short form of superintendent, a senior rank of police officer.

clue.text: Some can't take this instrument in vacuous version of Gershwin

indicators.note: the instrument is placed inside the emptied name
vacuous means empty, so the word loses everything but its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the composer's name
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark that some listeners cannot stand a hollow Gershwin rendition on the lute.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: coeliacs and others with an intolerance cannot take this protein. 'Version of' just joins the empty composer to the lute.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the wheat protein many people with coeliac disease or an intolerance must avoid eating.

clue.text: Mostly poor-quality time in gallery

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: lo-fi means low fidelity, of poor sound quality
T abbreviates time

explanation.surface: Someone spends mostly wasted time in an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is an upper gallery or balcony, as in a church organ loft.

clue.text: How can you say that heavy dieter needs to reform?

indicators.note: to reform is to remake something in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An indignant retort to the suggestion that an overweight slimmer must change their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses outraged disbelief at a remark, exactly like asking how anyone could say such a thing.

clue.text: Some paper every year has prominent coverage

indicators.note: being given coverage means being wrapped, so the outer word goes round the first piece

parts.note: noted means well-known or eminent
p.a. is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A newspaper gives big headline coverage to a story every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a newspaper; here it means writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of sheets for jotting on, so it is some paper.

clue.text: One scoring very quietly, turning into potential success

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: a comer is someone likely to succeed, an up-and-comer

indicators.note: turning round means facing back the other way, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
p is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A striker scores ever so softly, turning a chance into a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring' suggests football goals; it means writing a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music, setting it down as a score, so is one scoring.

clue.text: Complex leftover subplot is hindrance to shooting

indicators.note: complex suggests something intricate and tangled, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film critic grumbles that a tangled spare storyline holds up the shooting of the movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' reads as filming in the surface; in the definition it is gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Body armour stops bullets, so it hinders a gunman's attempt to wound the wearer.

clue.text: Picture of drunk swine hit hard

parts.note: lit is slang for intoxicated
a hog is a pig
to rap is to strike sharply
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tabloid scene: an image of a drunken brute of a man who punched someone hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithograph is a print made from a flat stone or plate, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Six-footer supporting short, snappy form of sport

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: testy means irritable and snappish
a cricket is an insect, with six feet

explanation.surface: A tall athlete backs a brisk, punchy version of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' looks like a tall person, but it is an insect with six legs. In a down answer, supporting means placed underneath. Test cricket is the five-day international format, the least snappy of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Test cricket is the longest international format of cricket, one form of the sport.

clue.text: Fibre of male politician

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A question of the moral fibre of a male politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is a plant whose stem yields a tough fibre used for rope and cloth.

clue.text: Parisian's very old hat put on king who's intrusive

definitions.note: read as one who's intrusive, a noun

parts.note: très is French for very
passé means out of date, old hat
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's ancient hat is placed on a monarch who barges in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for 'one who is intrusive'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser goes on to land without permission, intruding on someone's property.

clue.text: Grief acts to preclude love match

indicators.note: to preclude is to shut out, so the letter for love is excluded from the word

parts.note: does is a form of the verb to do, to act
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a pair is a matching couple

explanation.surface: A sad story: grief drives someone to rule out a marriage for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deep sorrow close to grief.

clue.text: Basic author's getting into short books

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

parts.note: short in the sense of curt or abrupt
the author's way of saying I am, as I'm
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A writer of basics sneaks into a set of slim volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short books' looks like one idea, but short is curt and books is the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a basic principle or element, so it can be called a basic.

clue.text: Went off violin entertaining you previously

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A fiddler wandered off while playing to an audience of days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander away from the proper path, so strayed means went off.

clue.text: Steaming tool was in the van

parts.note: a pick is a digging tool
being in the van is being at the front, leading

explanation.surface: Someone loaded a hot, steaming implement into their delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' is short for vanguard, the front; 'steaming' is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for being thoroughly intoxicated by alcohol.

clue.text: Wood welcoming you in

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them inside, so the wood holds the letter

parts.note: poplar is a tree and its timber
U is the text-message spelling of you

explanation.surface: A forest invites a visitor in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is fashionable and popular with most people.

clue.text: Lodges run without leader, anyway

indicators.note: the word must go without its leading letter, so its head is dropped

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
besides is used to mean in any case

explanation.surface: Masonic lodges keep going without a grand master in any case.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to live there, as one resides at an address.

clue.text: Crushes example of marital relations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: treads heavily on, squashes underfoot
second meaning: a relative acquired by marriage, a spouse's son

explanation.surface: Infatuations as one example of how married couples get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marital relations' suggests sex; it means relatives by marriage. Read as two words for the first meaning and one for the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a husband's or wife's son from an earlier union, one kind of relative by marriage.

clue.text: Two or three? Not quite precise

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: two and three are both prime numbers

explanation.surface: Someone asked to be exact hedges between two and three.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that two or three are examples of the answer, not a number to count.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim describes someone stiffly proper and fussy, exact in manners and correct behaviour.

clue.text: American right-wing slogan about left leading fellow to Unite

parts.note: A abbreviates American

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the slogan goes round the letter for left

parts.note: Make America Great Again, Trump's campaign slogan
L abbreviates left
a mate is a companion or chap

explanation.surface: A US campaign chant urging the political left and its leading man to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: To amalgamate is to merge separate things into one combined whole.

clue.text: Launch Times campaign

parts.note: to lob is to throw or launch in a high arc
by is used for multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: The newspaper starts a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to campaign to persuade politicians to support a cause.

clue.text: A fish jelly

parts.note: taken as written
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish set in aspic, as on a buffet table.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used to set food and grow bacterial cultures.

clue.text: Texan enthusiastically to enjoy joke about new men from Louisiana

definitions.note: an American idiom, so Texan flags the usage

parts.note: to enjoy something is to like it

indicators.note: about means going round, so the joke surrounds the letter for new

parts.note: a gag is a joke
N abbreviates new
buster is an American way of addressing a man, hence men from a US state

explanation.surface: A Texan heartily loves a joke about some newcomers from Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From Louisiana' tells you the men are addressed the American way, as busters; 'Texan' marks the definition as American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The US idiom means with great energy and vigour, so it describes doing something very enthusiastically.

clue.text: Bar could stock this food for someone who asks

parts.note: surface reading: a pub might keep this item of food on its menu
setter's reading: put this word inside the letters of bar and you get a word for a person who asks for alms

explanation.surface: A pub could keep this snack in for any customer who requests it.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: the answer placed inside BAR gives BEGGAR, someone who asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens' eggs are a basic everyday food, boiled, fried or scrambled.

clue.text: Give back wet vessel

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it in water
an urn is a vase or container

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to hand back a soggy container.
explanation.definitionFit: To return something is to hand it back to its owner.

clue.text: H from Steps ultimately removed from dry song he composed

indicators.note: composed as in written or arranged, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
what is removed from the following words is taken out of them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: last letter of the pop group's name

explanation.surface: Steps, the British pop group, had a dry song that someone wrote for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the song is the one removed. Steps were a British pop group of the late 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: H is the chemical symbol for the element hydrogen, the lightest gas.
